sentences.text: Tonganosaurus is a mamenchisaurid sauropod dinosaur named after the town of Tong'an in Sichuan, China, and is similar to Omeisaurus.
Its front limbs were shorter than its rear limbs, with a length ratio of 0.80, while the tibia was straight and thick, measuring 75% of the femur's length.
Based on comparisons with Omeisaurus, the skeleton is calculated to be 11.6 meters long, with an estimated living length of about 12 meters.
This dinosaur is the oldest known member of the mamenchisaurid family, existing almost 15 million years before the next-oldest members of the group.
The holotype is associated with Brontopodus footprints that may have been made by this taxon, suggesting it left such tracks.
The genus Tonganosaurus was established by Li et al. in 2010, with the type species designated as Tonganosaurus hei.
The holotype specimen is housed at the Chengdu University of Technology Museum under the catalog number MCDUT 14454.
Tonganosaurus is classified within the family Mamenchisauridae.
Tonganosaurus is believed to date from the late Early Jurassic (Pliensbachian) approximately 184.5 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
Plant fossils found with the dinosaur, dominated by the genus Aclistochara, suggest it lived in shallow-to-deep lake and flood environments.
The specific horizon of the specimen and the precise age of the Yimen Formation remain controversial among researchers.
